title: Dating the photo and the history of saxophone sections
summary: They guess the photo's date, and Harris describes how sax sections grew from three to four or five, and his section with Bartholomew.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: About what year was that photograph taken?
Well, I really know. You got me there. I couldn't really know.
There's nothing around the back. No, it doesn't. You were quite small at that time? I was really small, yeah.
But I mean, we'll mention it has three saxophones and tuba, piano, drums and banjo and one trumpet and one trombone. One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine. That was a good band.
It wouldn't have been too early with the three saxes. Hardly what? Before 1920 anyway, would it? No, no.

The most people was using around the 20s of the three saxophones. Right now they have addition now they're using five and four, you know? Yeah. That's what they're using now. Long time they used three. Two altos, baritone, two tenors and baritone. And some of them have two altos, two tenors and baritone. And when I, the last section we had, when we launched the band when I was with Dave, we had two saxophones and we had one altos player, he was dubbing on baritone and altos. And we had two tenors.
